[Source 1] LLM Evaluation Frameworks: HELM, BIG-Bench, and MMLU Benchmarks
tect. Dynamic benchmarks such as LiveBench (White et al., 2024) use freshly generated questions (math competitions, coding contests post-training-cutoff) to prevent contamination. MT-Bench (Zheng et al., 2023) uses GPT-4 as a judge to score multi-turn conversation quality across writing, roleplay, extraction, reasoning, math, coding, and STEM domains (scores 1-10). LLM-as-judge approaches show high correlation with human preferences (Spearman ρ≈0.9) but suffer from position bias (favoring first responses) and verbosity bias. Arena-style evaluation (Chatbot Arena, LMSYS) uses Elo ratings from millions of blind pairwise human preference votes, providing contamination-resistant evaluation at scale, with GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet, and Gemini 1.5 Pro consistently at the top.

[Source 3] Speculative Decoding for Accelerated LLM Inference
to serve as the draft mechanism, eliminating the need for a separate model and achieving 2.8x speedup on Vicuna-7B/13B. Self-speculative decoding uses earlier layers of the target model to generate draft tokens, achieving 1.4-1.8x speedup with zero additional parameters. Production deployments at scale use speculative decoding in various forms: Google uses a 7B model to accelerate Gemini Pro inference. The approach combines naturally with quantization, FlashAttention, and continuous batching (vLLM) for production LLM serving. Key limitations include sensitivity to draft-target model distribution match and reduced benefit at large batch sizes where compute utilization is already high.
